messages:
Maya: heads-up — Enterprise pilot customer wants a GA commitment window. They asked for an SLA, per-route billing, and a 24/7 emergency support window. Need product + eng + sales alignment today.

Devin: quick Q: what's their target latency and what models/seq len are in play?

Maya: p99 < 200ms for 256 tokens, p95 < 120ms. Models: M-family (lm-v2) + potential quantized variants. Primary region EU with occasional US fallback.

Sam: that p99 is ambitious on shared hosted pools. Two paths: (1) Dedicated pools with multi-AZ + pinned nodes = feasible, (2) hosted with reserved burst capacity + fallback to lower-latency variants but tail risk remains.

Taylor: pricing implication — per-route token accounting + 24/7 emergency support suggests either a new premium SLA SKU or an addon surcharge. Need finops input.

Priya (sales): revenue context: pilot contract ~$250k ARR first year, strategic account for EU expansion. They're asking for a straightforward 3-line commitment they can put in an MSA.

Kelly: legal will need the exact SLA definition + credit calc. Also confirm what counts as outage vs degradation (errors vs latency).

Devin: monitoring ask: we should require per-route dashboards, continuous p50/p95/p99, burn rate alerting when error budget >50% used, and a 1-minute-aggregation health metric for auto-rollback. Also sampling for quality drift.

Sam: engineering ops checklist (high level):
- define model variants & seq distribution
- infra plan for Dedicated + autoscale testing
- fallback mapping (primary -> quantized -> smaller model)
- synthetic load tests + SLO verification
- oncall escalation playbook for pilot

Maya: docs/runbook: onboarding doc + SRE runbook + escalation matrix + expected behavior table (fallback quality deltas, token billing examples). Target: docs ready at handoff for pilot launch.

Taylor: prioritization note — supporting this pilot will move Optimize backlog by ~2 sprints. Is commercial justification sufficient?

Priya (sales): yes, customer will convert to enterprise contract if pilot meets SLA. High probability.

Sam: rough eng estimates: infra work 3w (2 infra engs), runtime & fallback 2w (1 runtime eng), SLA testing + burn-in 1w. Docs and legal prep in parallel 1w. Overall ~5 weeks with parallelization.

Maya: propose two options for the customer:
A) Dedicated Pilot Offer: 99.9% availability SLA (p99 latency objective), per-route token billing, 24/7 emergency support (phone + pager), contractual SLA credits, faster launch (~5w)
B) Hosted Pilot Offer: conservative SLA (99.5%), burst addon for reserved capacity, region-aware routing, limited emergency support (business hours + on-call escalation), longer validation runway (~8+ wks)

Kelly: legal asks for SLA credit formula & exclusions. We should include force majeure, scheduled maintenance windows, and customer misconfiguration exclusions.

Devin: operational guardrails: require initial traffic shaping (ramp to baseline qps over 48h), pre-approved test harness, and a rollback rule: if p99 > target for 10m sustained, trigger failover to canary/rollback + pager.

Sam: testing plan: 1) lab synthetic tests for seq len profiles, 2) staging soak with production-like traffic, 3) pilot shadowing, 4) production cutover under guarded ramp. Need customer payload samples and model versions by EOD.

Maya: timeline ask: can owners commit to a spec doc + action plan in 48 hours? I'll coordinate and own spec + runbook draft.

Taylor: I'll run pricing scenarios (SKU vs addon) and present quick revenue/COGS delta.

Priya (sales): I'll prepare contract skeleton and liaise with customer legal. Need SLA bullets to include ASAP.

Kelly: Legal will draft credit clause once SLA numbers are finalized. Please don't bake in unlimited credits.

oncall-bot: created ticket PILOT-9123 "Enterprise pilot SLA and GA readiness" assigned: @Sam, @Devin

Sam: noted. I'll start infra spike for pinned pools + latency profiling. Need access to customer sample traces and a clear seq length histogram.

Devin: I'll sketch the monitoring dashboard and alerting thresholds. Will include an SLO burn rate alarm and auto-escalation steps.

Maya: Great — next sync in 48hrs. Action owners: Maya (spec & runbook), Sam (infra + tests), Devin (monitoring + rollback rules), Taylor (pricing), Priya (contract), Kelly (legal review).

Maya: closing note — if we pick Option A, we should be explicit about limited availability (pilot capacity), rollout sequencing, and an exit criteria for the customer if SLA not met. :white_check_mark:

Priya (sales): customer is comfortable with a pilot window and explicit exit criteria. Will confirm contract language. :ok_hand:

Sam: will post initial latency profiles to this thread once available.

Maya: thanks all; reconvene in 48hrs.
